fieldValues.title: Huge unknown integers in a registry are refused, not rounded
fieldValues.decision_question: When exact numeric comparison (RFC-056 [R4]) makes the registry loader meet an integer beyond u64 in an unknown field, does it refuse the registry or round the number?
fieldValues.context: srs-rust#1716 enables serde_json's arbitrary_precision workspace-wide so field filters compare decimals exactly, as RFC-056 [R4] requires. As a side effect, the srs-core Registry refuses to load an integer beyond u64 in an unknown field (serde's flatten buffer has no u128) instead of rounding it silently. The TPR reviewer escalated it: a behaviour change no ruling covered.
fieldValues.friction: Without a ruling the PR could not merge: merging would presume the answer.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: (1) Keep the refusal: no silent corruption; a registry carrying such a number fails to load. (2) Do nothing: revert to f64; RFC-056 [R4] stays violated for decimals and the registry rounds silently. (3) A custom deserializer that carries such numbers through flatten: exact and loadable, at the cost of code no current case needs.
fieldValues.key_requirements: RFC-056 [R4]: exact numeric comparison. No silent corruption. Build only what a current requirement needs.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The registry refuses an integer beyond u64 in an unknown field rather than rounding it silently.
fieldValues.rationale: Owner, 2026-11-27: 'This implements the current feature and we can revisit when we hit a requirement.' The refusal is loud, the exactness is what the ruling asks for, no known registry carries such a number, and undoing it means reverting one Cargo feature.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A real registry carries an integer beyond u64 in an unknown field.
